conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve had watery diarrhea for about two weeks now. I just feel weak and unwell. I’m not eating much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fevers, nausea, or blood in the stool?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fevers or vomiting. The stool is watery but not bloody. I do have some pain on my right side, near my ribs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Given your history of transplant and GVHD, we need to be careful about infections or other causes. We’ll run some stool tests.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on a lot of meds. Could one of them be causing this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. We noticed you were on metoclopramide four times a day before. That can cause diarrhea. We’ve reduced it to twice daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, I didn’t know that. That might explain it. But I’ve had this for two weeks—shouldn’t it have stopped by now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can take a few days. We’ll monitor. We also did a chest X-ray today—looks clear, no pneumonia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good to hear. My back’s been better since I got the brace last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your T11 fracture and disc herniations are being managed well with the brace and pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are stable. We’re waiting on stool tests to rule out infections like C. diff or parasites.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any results yet?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. But your abdominal exam is soft, no severe tenderness, which is reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I did feel a bit dizzy when I stood up yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the nurse noted orthostatic hypotension. We gave you a liter of fluids, and your blood pressure improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I’ve had that before. Is it serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s common in patients like you, especially with reduced intake. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your stool tests came back. No C. diff, no salmonella, no parasites. All negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not an infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unlikely. The GI team thinks it could be small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, especially with your history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What’s that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It means too many bacteria in the small intestine, which can cause diarrhea. They suggested an antibiotic called rifaximin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, can I take that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We tried, but your insurance denied it. We’ll schedule a GI follow-up in a month to discuss other options.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s frustrating. What can I do in the meantime?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Stay hydrated, eat small bland meals, and we’ll keep using loperamide if needed. Your diarrhea has improved, hasn’t it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s much better since I’ve been here. Maybe it was the metoclopramide.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your liver tests are a bit elevated, but they’ve always been that way due to GVHD, so no new concern.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my sirolimus? I heard it might need adjusting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your level was high. We’ve reduced your dose from 1.5 mg to 1 mg daily to stay in the safe range.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will that affect my GVHD control?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We don’t expect so. Your prednisone is still helping. We’ll check the level again as an outpatient.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. What about my pancreas cysts? I remember they said to follow up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the MRCP showed small cysts, likely benign. You’ll need another scan in six months to monitor them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. No diarrhea today. We’re thinking about discharge tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Will I need any more tests before I leave?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your bloodwork this morning. Hemoglobin is low, but stable. You’ve had anemia for a while.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I always feel a bit tired. Is there anything we can do?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep monitoring. Iron studies were normal, so it’s likely related to chronic disease. No transfusion needed now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my blood thinner? I remember I had another clot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you have a small clot in your right leg. You’ll stay on enoxaparin 40 mg daily, same as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it a new clot or old?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s unclear—could be recanalizing old clot. But with your history, we’re keeping you on anticoagulation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge today. You’ve been off diarrhea, labs are stable, and pain is controlled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep taking your meds as listed. The visiting nurse will help you with injections and meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the sirolimus level?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, get it checked before your morning dose, as instructed. Also, follow up with GI in a month.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the pancreas scan?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Schedule the MRCP in six months. Call radiology to set it up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Call if diarrhea returns or you feel lightheaded. Otherwise, take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming—you’re cleared to go home. The nurse will go over your meds one more time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve got the list. I’ll follow up on all the tests.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll see you in follow-up. Take it easy, and wear your back brace as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for taking such good care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Get some rest and stay hydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, one last thing—should I avoid any foods?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Stick to low-fat, easy-to-digest foods for now. Avoid heavy or greasy meals that might upset your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. No fried food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And keep using the loperamide only if diarrhea comes back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Understood. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re all set. The transport team will take you home shortly.
